raw.jobDescription:
Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution.

The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing.

This is a technical management role to lead a team that develops Python and Golang micro-services that power our global software distribution engine. The world sees it as the Snap Store and Charmhub.io marketplaces, behind the scenes it is a unified system that understands key concepts in software distribution - architectures, releases, betas, release candidates, stable releases, branches and more. We are on a journey to transform the experience that people all over the world have with their open source software by significantly expanding the range of software we can deliver through this system. If you have a passion for clean APIs, believe that great engineers ship software calmly and regularly against an agile plan, and know that tests are the key to higher velocity and reliability, you'll fit right in.

This is a great opportunity to take part in engineering a highly scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance). In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.

As an Engineering Manager at Canonical, you must be technically strong, but your main responsibility is to run an effective team and develop the colleagues you manage. You will develop and review code as a leader, but know that the best way to improve the product is to ensure that the whole team is focused, productive and unblocked. You are expected to help them grow as engineers, do meaningful work, do it outstandingly well, find professional and personal satisfaction, and work well with colleagues and the community. You will also be expected to be a positive influence on culture, facilitate technical delivery, and regularly reflect with your team on strategy and execution. You will collaborate closely with other Engineering Managers, product managers, and architects, producing an engineering roadmap with ambitious and achievable goals.

We expect Engineering Managers to be fluent in the programming language, architecture, and components that their team uses. Code reviews and architectural leadership are part of the job. The commitment to healthy engineering practices, documentation, quality and performance optimisation is as important, as is the requirement for fair and clear management, and the obligation to ensure a high-performing team.

This is a great opportunity to really learn how to do engineering of a highly-scalable SaaS product (think about the load on our systems when one of our largest Ubuntu Desktop snaps is updated by the publisher, for instance). In addition, you will have the opportunity to learn from Canonical's world-class security team as we work collectively to deliver this capability, safely, to our customers around the world.

Location: This role may be based remotely in the Americas, Europe, Middle East or Africa time zones.

What your day will look like

  • Lead a remote team of engineers in your time zone
  • Develop talent through coaching, mentoring, feedback, and hands-on career development
  • Set and manage expectations with other engineering teams, management, and external stakeholders
  • Be an active part of the leadership team and collaborate with other leaders in the organisation
  • With your team, build clean web service APIs to support both CLI and web frontend clients, using Python (and optionally Golang).
  • Engage with many other teams at Canonical, as well as the open-source community and commercial partners

What we are looking for in you

  • Good experience in leading modern, agile software development practices
  • Experience in forming a healthy, collaborative engineering culture in line with the company values
  • Demonstrative experience of being a role model for sound engineering principles and directly contributing toward your team's goals
  • Willingness to travel up to 4 times a year for internal events
  • You love to mentor, develop and grow people, and have a track record of doing it
  • You are knowledgeable and passionate about software development
  • You are focused on success and the timely delivery of high-quality software
  • You value and nurture great team culture and spirit
  • You have experience and commitment to agile development methodologies
  • Software development experience in Python (experience in Golang in addition to that would be a big plus)
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Practical experience with Linux system administration

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce.

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

  • Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!
  • Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum
  • Annual compensation review
  • Recognition rewards
  • Annual holiday leave
  • Parental leave
  • Employee Assistance Programme
  • Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’
  • Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

About Canonical

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open-source projects and the platform for AI, IoT, and the cloud, we are changing the world of software. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence; in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do. Most colleagues at Canonical have worked from home since our inception in 2004.​ Working here is a step into the future and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game.

Canonical is an equal opportunity employer

We are proud to foster a workplace free from discrimination. Diversity of experience, perspectives, and background create a better work environment and better products. Whatever your identity, we will give your application fair consideration.

raw.jobDescription:
This is a permanent full-time remote opportunity for those based in the UK.

About Nearform

Nearform is an independent team of data & AI experts, engineers, and designers who build intelligent digital solutions and capability at pace. We create AI-enabled solutions that enhance digital experiences, empower developers, and deliver measurable results. In these ways, we partner with ambitious enterprises to deliver enduring impact.

Our deep expertise in solving the world’s most complex digital problems, along with our collaborative, people-first approach, enables enterprises to build breakthrough products and modernise legacy systems by unleashing the power of AI.

Today, our team of 500 experts in 20+ countries is trusted by leading enterprises including Lululemon, Puma, Sun Life, Starbucks, Travelex, Virgin Media 02, and Walmart.

As part of our Engineering function, you will work closely with clients to translate complex business requirements into innovative digital products.

Whether you are a Senior Engineer, Tech Lead, or DevOps Engineer, you will collaborate with distributed teams, leveraging cutting-edge technologies to build secure, high-performance applications. Our Nearform engineers are known for building high quality, scalable solutions that solve real world problems.

About the Senior Golang Engineer role

As a Senior Engineer at Nearform your main task will be designing & building applications using Golang. However as you’ll likely work on a variety of projects your responsibilities may also include:

  • Supporting component design, development and maintenance and taking responsibility for personal technical quality standards within the project team.
  • Assisting with defining structured practices, especially in source code management, building and deployment.
  • Designing and implementing data storage solutions.
  • Optimising performance in applications for maximum speed and scalability.
  • Getting feedback from users and clients, and building solutions for them.
  • Assisting with the analysis of client requirements.
  • Working with and supporting Technical Leaders in project execution and timely delivery.
  • Collaborating with client teams.

What we are looking for in this person

  • Significant experience delivering at a Senior Engineer level. Our Seniors typically have at least 6 years’ commercial experience.
  • Practical experience of delivering in an agile environment.
  • Practical experience and knowledge of developing real-world solutions.
  • Deep knowledge of Golang.
  • Working on K8s is essential.
  • Python experience is highly desirable.
  • Deep understanding of versioning control tools - e.g. Git.
  • Testing experience and familiarity with testing tools at all levels, unit, integration and end to end testing.
  • Practical and real world experience working with databases and cloud environments.
  • Experience with automation, CI and CD.
  • Experience building software collaboratively using pull requests and code reviews
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
  • Professional proficiency in English.

Benefits and Perks we offer at Nearform

  • Annual Company Bonus - We all help Nearform to hit company goals so we all receive a share of the profits on an annual basis in line with company performance.
  • Work Remotely and Flexibly - We have a genuine dedication to work/life balance. Our flexible working culture allows you to work around what matters - school run, no problem!
  • Paid Time Off Package - We offer an annual leave of 25 days plus public holidays. We also offer sick leave, marriage leave and many more.
  • Remote Working Allowance - Every 2 years, you will have a budget of up to €1250 (equivalent in GBP) to help you set up a comfortable and productive workspace in addition to your essential equipment provided by Nearform when you join.
  • Training and Development Allowance - We understand the importance of continuously learning so we offer an allowance of up to €1000 (equivalent in GBP) you can use to upskill yourself.
  • Healthcare - It’s important to always take care of your health, so we offer additional private healthcare here at Nearform. If you wish to learn more about the plan offered feel free to reach out to our team.
  • Pension & Insurances - We offer a pension match of up to 5% and Income Protection and Death in Service for peace of mind.

Our Interview Process

  • Talent Call (30 mins via Zoom)
    An introductory conversation with a member of our Talent Team to learn more about your background, experience, and career goals. We'll also provide a high-level overview of Nearform and answer any questions you may have. This step helps us assess initial alignment.
  • Technical Assessment (1 hour via Zoom)
    A live coding challenge with one of our trained interviewers. You'll be asked to build a working solution to a problem via screen sharing, demonstrating your Golang, problem-solving ability, and coding best practices in a real-time environment.
  • Hiring Manager Interview (45 mins via Zoom)
    A conversation with a Hiring Manager focused on your approach to teamwork, client collaboration, and problem-solving in an enterprise development setting. We'll also share more details about Nearform and the potential projects you may join.

There may also be an additional interview with the client depending on the project.

Ready to Join Us?

If you're passionate about building high-quality applications, solving complex challenges, and driving innovation in enterprise development, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now via our careers page at Nearform and be part of a team that values technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous learning.

Nearform is committed to shaping a better world in all that we do. Our global team is built based on respect, inclusivity, diversity and excellence.

If you require any adjustments to the interview process as part of your application, please let someone from our Talent Team know so they can help.

Our salary range starts from £75,000 + bonus & benefits and will be discussed during the initial interview based on your experience.

As part of our recruitment process, we conduct manual and electronic identity verification checks to confirm the identity of prospective employees.

About us

The rapid transition to electric vehicles (EVs) is the biggest change in transportation since the Model T. Flipturn is building the EV charging and energy platform for the next generation of sustainable transportation. We're already working with the largest forward-thinking Fortune 500 EV fleets across trucking, transit, and autonomous.

Flipturn is now a part of Einride, a global company revolutionizing transportation by showing the world a new way to move, based on the latest digital, electric and autonomous technologies. Through a suite of EV charging and fleet solutions and freight capacity as a service operations, Einride enables businesses around the world to accelerate towards their sustainability goals. Einride’s customers include some of the world’s biggest shippers, including Fortune 500 companies.

At Flipturn, you’ll:

  • Build a climate/sustainability-focused product, working on projects that directly impact real-life EV infrastructure

  • Collaborate with a team of extremely talented and mission-driven teammates (Stripe, Samsara, Google, MIT, UC Berkeley)

  • Work with modern technologies and best in class tools (ex: Yocto, TypeScript, GraphQL, AWS, Cursor, Claude)

  • Build for the long term as part of Einride, a global leader in EV and autonomous transportation technology

The role

This role is focused on the Flipturn Controller, a cutting-edge onsite control computer that integrates with EV chargers, batteries, generators, meters, and utility programs. You'll be involved in building major features, getting feedback from customers, driving the vision of our EV charging platform, and setting the culture of our engineering team.

You'll work on projects like:

  • Integrating EV charging with on-site batteries and generators, utility programs, and other sources of control

  • Upgrading our embedded Linux systems, including build tooling (Yocto or similar), bootloaders, and board bring-up

  • Firmware and full-stack improvements to Flipturn's innovative energy management platform, for example helping customers participate in PG&E's Flex Connect program to get their sites up and running faster

We're looking for people who have:

  • 4-7 years of experience in software engineering

  • 2+ years of experience with firmware development

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems – build tooling (Yocto or similar), bootloaders, and board bring-up

  • Interest in working on firmware/hardware projects as well as full-stack product development, as needed to deliver a fully working end-to-end product

  • Experience on a fast-moving industry-leading technology team and delivering products and features end-to-end

  • Interest in using AI tools to accelerate software development

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation: The anticipated range for this position is $190,000 - $230,000 base salary per year, with an additional equity component

  • Comprehensive health coverage: Medical, dental, and vision plans, including PPO and HSA options.

  • Retirement savings: 401(k) plan with an employer match.

  • Generous time off: 25 days of Paid Time Off (PTO). 15 paid sick days and 15 paid US holidays observed.

  • Wellness allowance: To support your personal well-being.

  • Offices in NYC and Austin, as well as regular team bonding weeks with remote team members

title: Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer CCS – Europäische Standardisierung EU-Rail (50%)
description: Im Rahmen des europäischen Projekts «Europäische Standardisierung CCS-Strecke» arbeiten gemeinsam mit führenden internationalen Bahnindustrieunternehmen wie Siemens, Hitachi, Alstom und CAF sowie europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern wie DB, SNCF, RFI, ÖBB, Network Rail und ProRail an der Weiterentwicklung und Harmonisierung zukünftiger Bahnsysteme. Das Projekt ist Teil des Europe’s Rail Joint Undertaking (ERJU) und umfasst den System Pillar sowie den Innovation Pillar. Ziel ist die Entwicklung europaweit einheitlicher Betriebsprozesse, Systemarchitekturen und technischer Spezifikationen für die zukünftigen ERTMS-Zielsysteme, insbesondere ETCS Level 2 und Automatic Train Operation (ATO GoA 1/2). Die erarbeiteten Standards bilden die Grundlage für zukünftige europäische Betriebsvorschriften sowie für die Weiterentwicklung und Beschaffung von Sicherungsanlagen. Zur Unterstützung der internationalen Projektarbeiten suchen wir eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit als Senior Business Analyst / System Engineer im Bereich Control, Command and Signalling (CCS). System Engineering: Erarbeitung und Weiterentwicklung von Systemdefinitionen, Systemarchitekturen und technischen Systemspezifikationen im sicherheitsrelevanten Bahnumfeld (CCS). Spezifikationserstellung: Entwicklung und Abstimmung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen unter Berücksichtigung der Gesamtarchitektur sowie zukünftiger Bahnprozesse. Prozesskoordination: Verantwortung für die effiziente Umsetzung und kontinuierliche Optimierung der Arbeitsprozesse (Workstations) zur Erstellung der Systemspezifikationen. Operative Projektunterstützung: Unterstützung bei der Organisation, Koordination und Umsetzung der internationalen Arbeitsorganisation. Qualitätssicherung: Sicherstellung einer konsistenten, vollständigen und qualitativ hochwertigen Integration der Arbeitsergebnisse in die übergeordneten Systemspezifikationen. Stakeholder-Management: Zusammenarbeit und Abstimmung mit internationalen Industriepartnern, europäischen Infrastrukturbetreibern sowie internen und externen Fachspezialisten. Standardisierung: Mitwirkung bei der Entwicklung europäisch harmonisierter Betriebsprozesse und technischer Standards für zukünftige ERTMS-Systeme. Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium (ETH, Universität oder Fachhochschule) in Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einem verwandten naturwissenschaftlichen Fachgebiet. Umfassende Kenntnisse des Bahnsystems, insbesondere des Bahnbetriebs und der Zugsteuerung. Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Bereich internationale Standardisierung im Bahnumfeld. Fundierte Erfahrung in der Erstellung von System- und Schnittstellenspezifikationen im europäischen Umfeld. Erfahrung mit Application Lifecycle Management Tools, insbesondere Polarion. Ausgeprägte Kommunikationsfähigkeit sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Inhalte verständlich und zielgruppengerecht zu vermitteln. Sicheres Auftreten im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen nationalen und internationalen Stakeholdern. Sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. description: Für ein anspruchsvolles Mandat suchen wir einen erfahrenen Professional Software Engineer / Senior Fullstack Developer mit fundierten Kenntnissen in Java und Angular. Agile Entwicklung: Umsetzung von User Stories und technischen Anforderungen in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Entwicklern, Business Analysten und Fachvertretern. Systemintegration: Weiterentwicklung und Integration bestehender Anwendungen sowie Mitarbeit an der Ausrichtung von ZIS/FOS auf den TSI-TEL-Standard und die Integration in TMS (CM1). Datenverarbeitung: Entwicklung und Betreuung ereignisgesteuerter Systeme unter Einsatz von Kafka und MongoDB. DevOps und Betrieb: Sicherstellung des stabilen Betriebs, Unterhalts und der kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung der Anwendungen. Testing und Dokumentation: Erstellung und Pflege technischer Dokumentationen sowie Vorbereitung und Durchführung von Tests. Support: Analyse und Behebung technischer Störungen sowie Unterstützung der Anwender. Agile Zusammenarbeit: Aktive Mitarbeit in Scrum- und SAFe-Teams sowie kontinuierliche Verbesserung der Entwicklungsprozesse. Technische Verantwortung: Übernahme von Verantwortung für technische Themenbereiche und Unterstützung weniger erfahrener Teammitglieder. Mindestens 3 Jahre Berufserfahrung als Fullstack Developer mit Java und TypeScript. Fundierte Kenntnisse in Java, Spring Boot und Angular. Erfahrung mit modernen Entwicklungsstandards, Frameworks und Best Practices im Java- und Angular-Umfeld. Praktische Erfahrung mit OpenShift oder vergleichbaren Kubernetes-basierten Plattformen. Verständnis für event-driven Architekturen und die Herausforderungen verteilter Systeme. Erfahrung mit agilen Entwicklungsmethoden, insbesondere Scrum und SAFe. Praktische Erfahrung in CI/CD-Umgebungen (Continuous Integration / Continuous Deployment). Ausgeprägtes Sicherheitsbewusstsein in der Softwareentwicklung (Secure Software Development). Selbstständige, verantwortungsbewusste und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise. Teamfähigkeit, Kommunikationsstärke und Bereitschaft, Wissen aktiv im Team weiterzugeben. Hohe Lernbereitschaft und Interesse an neuen Technologien und Entwicklungsmustern. Deutsch: mindestens C1 Englisch: mindestens B1 Erfahrung im Bahn- bzw. Transportumfeld. title: Senior Full Stack Developer TypeScript (Vue / NestJS) (w/m/d) 80-100%
description: Jobbeschreibung Mach mit uns Schweizer Kleinunternehmen noch erfolgreicher! Klingt nach einer grossen Vision? Genau das treibt uns jeden Tag an. Wir bei bexio leben die Philosophie, dass erstklassige, effiziente und smarte Softwarelösungen für jedes KMU zugänglich und erschwinglich sein müssen. Mit dieser Mission sind wir heute die führende Anbieterin für webbasierte Business-Software in der Schweiz. Unser Expansionskurs geht steil nach oben: Über 100'000 zufriedene Kunden, mehr als 7'000 Treuhand-Partner und ein starkes Team von über 150 motivierten Mitarbeitenden sprechen für sich. Um diese Erfolgsgeschichte weiterzuschreiben, suchen wir tatkräftige Unterstützung. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel! Stellenanforderungen Was du bei uns bewegst Als Senior Developer übernimmst du die technische Verantwortung für unseren TypeScript-Stack, mit Vue.js im Frontend und Node.js/NestJS im Backend und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung von Kontera massgeblich mit. Du konzipierst, implementierst, testest und wartest Produkt-Features End-to-End: von der Benutzeroberfläche über die APIs bis hin zur Datenbank. Du triffst fundierte technische Entscheidungen, um skalierbare und wartbare Software zu entwickeln unter anderem für KI-gestützte Verarbeitungen und asynchrone Workflows. Du erweiterst unsere Integrationen mit Drittsystemen wie Banken, Zahlungsdienstleistern und Buchhaltungslösungen (einschliesslich bexio). Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produktmanagement sowie anderen Teams zusammen und vermittelst komplexe technische Zusammenhänge für alle verständlich. Durch das frühzeitige Erkennen und proaktive Minimieren technischer und projektbezogener Risiken stellst du reibungslose Entwicklungsprozesse über alle Phasen hinweg sicher. Du schreibst Clean Code für nachhaltige, hochgradig zuverlässige Software und teilst dein Wissen aktiv im Team, beispielsweise im Rahmen von Code-Reviews. Dein Rucksack für diese Stelle Du verfügst über mehr als 5 Jahre relevante Berufserfahrung als Software-Entwickler mit TypeScript, sowohl im Frontend als auch im Backend. Du entwickelst performante Single-Page-Applications mit inklusive sauberer API-Anbindungen an Node.js-Backends. Du hast fundierte Erfahrung in der Backend-Entwicklung mit Node.js, idealerweise mit NestJS, sowie im Design von REST-APIs (inklusive OAuth 2.0). Nachweisbare Kompetenz im Entwerfen und Treffen strategischer Entscheidungen für anspruchsvolle Softwarearchitekturen zeichnet dich aus. Du hast Routine im Schreiben von Clean Code sowie in Frontend- und Backend-Tests. Du bringst umfassende Praxiserfahrung mit relationalen Datenbanken (PostgreSQL) und asynchroner Verarbeitung mittels Task-Queues oder Messaging-Systemen mit. Du besitzt ein ausgeprägtes Verständnis für Websicherheit (z. B. OWASP Top 10, sichere Authentifizierung und Autorisierung) sowie den Schutz sensibler Finanz- und Personendaten. Du bringst fundierte Erfahrung in agilen Arbeitsumgebungen mit. Du fühlst dich in einer Team-First-Kultur mit starker Zusammenarbeit, Selbstreflexion und proaktiver Denkweise wohl. Darauf kannst du dich freuen Hybrid-Modell und Arbeitszeiten, die sich deinem Leben anpassen. 5 Wochen Ferien plus Option auf unbezahlten Urlaub. Yoga, Bootcamps, Massagen und legendäre Grill-Sessions. 16 Wochen Mutterschafts- und 3 Wochen Vaterschaftsurlaub. bexio übernimmt 63 % deiner Pensionskassenbeiträge – für mehr Netto vom Lohn. title: Data Platform Manager
description: About the role As Data Platform Manager you will own Destinus's company data platform. Built on Microsoft Fabric, it brings together data from our different systems, and it serves the reporting and data agents that production, supply chain, program management, and finance work from every week. You will own its architecture: how OneLake and our lakehouses are structured, how data lands in them from the systems we run, and how it holds up as more of the business comes to depend on it. You will lead a small team of data engineers — setting direction, reviewing their work, growing them — and you will keep building yourself. You are also the person who makes our AI ambitions possible: the foundation behind our data agents and our Company Brain is yours to design and deliver. At Destinus we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing, building advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) across three European plants. The data you will work with is physical — parts, build progress, shortages, non-conformances — and the questions asked of it get harder each year as we grow. If you want a platform you can still shape rather than one already set in concrete, this is a good moment to arrive. What You'll Do Own the architecture of our Microsoft Fabric estate end to end — OneLake, our lakehouses and their bronze, silver, and gold layers, workspace and domain structure, naming conventions, and the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Lead, mentor, and grow a small team of data engineers: set priorities, review code, raise the technical bar, and develop the people. Stay hands-on. You will build pipelines, notebooks, and Delta tables yourself, not only direct others who do. Own the integrations that land data in OneLake from our source systems — ERP, HR, shopfloor, quality, and the business applications that come after them — choosing sensibly between Data Factory pipelines, dataflows, shortcuts, and mirroring for each source. Own the gold layer and the semantic models built on it, so that Power BI reads from one governed source rather than from copies scattered around the business. Work closely with our Business Operations & Data Specialists, who represent the business owners of each domain: turn their requirements into the right gold tables, agree definitions with them, and give them a platform they can query, validate, and explain to the business with confidence. Own lineage across the estate: know what feeds what, be able to prove it to an auditor, and make dependencies visible rather than tribal knowledge. Build the data foundation for our AI programme — the lakehouse structures, pipelines, and knowledge graph behind our Fabric data agents and our Company Brain — and deliver it to a standard that can be trusted with a real question. Design and maintain the OneLake security and access model together with your team: workspace roles, access groups, and the controls that decide who sees what in the lake. Keep the platform reliable, observable, and cost-aware: monitoring, alerting, recovery, and disciplined use of our Fabric capacity — including knowing what a runaway notebook costs us. Requirements What You’ll Need Requirements Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Engineering, or a related field. 5-8 years of data engineering experience, including real ownership of a lakehouse architecture rather than only delivering against someone else's. Hands-on Microsoft Fabric experience is strongly preferred — OneLake, lakehouses, Delta tables, the SQL analytics endpoint, Data Factory pipelines, Spark notebooks, and semantic models in Direct Lake mode. If your depth is in Azure Synapse, Databricks, or Data Lake Storage Gen2 and you have since moved onto Fabric in earnest, we will take that seriously. Strong command of the medallion pattern and of Delta Lake in practice: partitioning, schema evolution, table maintenance, and why a gold table behaves the way it does. Genuinely hands-on. Strong SQL, solid PySpark, and comfort building and orchestrating pipelines yourself. This is not a role that stops at diagrams. Practical understanding of Fabric capacity: how workloads consume it, how to spot what is burning it, and how to keep the platform inside its envelope. Experience leading engineers — formally, or as a technical lead who set direction and mentored others. A first step into people management is welcome if the technical leadership is already there. Proven integration experience with ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, as well as APIs, flat-file landings, and change data capture from operational databases. Solid data modelling skills, including dimensional modelling and an understanding of how a semantic layer serves Power BI. Working knowledge of lineage, data governance, and access control in a cloud platform; exposure to Microsoft Purview is a plus. Interest or experience in the data foundations behind AI assistants — retrieval, knowledge graphs, and preparing data so that an agent can answer with it. Aerospace or another regulated industry is an advantage; so is experience in a start-up or scale-up. Fluent in English; additional European languages are a plus. Who You Are You are an architect who never stops building. You have strong opinions about how a platform should be structured, and you earn the right to them by being in the code. You would rather make a design decision explicit and documented than let it live in one person's head. You care more about reliability than novelty. You know that the measure of a data platform is whether people trust the numbers that come out of it on a Monday morning, not how modern the stack looks on a slide. When something breaks, you want to know why it was possible, not just how to patch it. You enjoy growing engineers, and you understand that leading a small team means doing the work alongside them. Above all, you want to build something durable — a foundation that holds while the company scales on top of it. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Business Operations & Data Specialist (Production & Quality)
description: About the role Behind every well-run plant is a shared understanding of how it is performing — and that understanding has to be built. As a Business Operations & Data Specialist focused on Production & Quality at Destinus, you are the bridge between the people who run our plants and the data that describes them. Plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers own the processes; our lakehouse holds the data those processes create. Your job is to connect the two, so that every production and quality figure, from the shopfloor to the leadership team, is defined by the business, built on the lakehouse, and trusted by both. This is as much an operations role as a reporting one. You will translate what the business needs to know into what the data platform has to deliver, working with our Data Engineers on the production and quality data in the lakehouse and turning it into the reporting used across three European plants, including our Digital Shopfloor Management Solution, relied on by more than 300 people. You will also go to where the data is created and make it better there — improving how it is captured, automating what is still manual, and helping three plants work to one standard. At Destinus, we are redefining the future of aerospace manufacturing — bringing speed, precision, and innovation to every process that powers our advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our operations span multiple plants and teams, and your work will directly support the reliability, efficiency, and excellence required for mission-critical production. Join us in shaping the next era of aerospace operations. What You'll do Be the go-to contact between the business owners of production and quality data — plant managers, production leads, and quality engineers — and our lakehouse: turn their questions into clear data requirements, and the data back into answers they can act on. Own the production and quality portfolio end to end: define the KPI, improve the process behind it, build the dashboard, and stand behind the number. Own the production and quality domain in our lakehouse: know which tables and fields hold what, where each comes from, and who owns it at source — and keep that knowledge documented rather than in your head. Partner with our Data Engineers on the curated (gold) layer for production and quality: specify the tables, fields, and business rules the business needs, and validate the result against what actually happens on the shopfloor before anyone relies on it. Set and monitor data quality checks for your domain, and route each issue to the right owner — the person entering the data, the system configuration, or the pipeline — until it is fixed. Maintain and continuously improve Power BI dashboards tracking production and quality performance across all three plants, built on certified lakehouse data rather than side spreadsheets. Describe production and quality data in plain business language — what each field means, who owns it, and how sensitive it is — for our shared meanings layer, so that colleagues and our AI assistants can use it correctly without having to ask you first. Automate what is manual today: recurring reports, data collection, and the preparation behind daily and weekly performance routines. Support the standardisation of ways of working across the three plants, partnering with our Lean Operations Specialist so that measurement and improvement pull in the same direction. Requirements What You’ll Need Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Quality Management, or a related field. Experience in a production or quality environment; aerospace or another regulated industry is highly preferred. Solid understanding of manufacturing and quality metrics — throughput, cycle time, OEE, scrap and rework, first-pass yield — and of quality processes such as non-conformance handling, customer complaints and field returns, root cause analysis, and corrective actions. Strong expertise in Power BI (data modeling, DAX, dashboard design, troubleshooting), complemented by advanced Excel skills. Comfortable querying data with SQL and working in a lakehouse or data warehouse environment; experience with Microsoft Fabric or a medallion (bronze/silver/gold) architecture is a plus. You will not build the pipelines — you need to know what to ask for and how to check what comes back. Able to explain data to non-technical colleagues and business needs to technical ones — and to get both sides to agree on one definition. Knowledge of ERP systems such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 / MSD, and familiarity with shopfloor or MES systems. A track record of improving or automating a process, not only reporting on it. Exposure to continuous improvement methods is a plus. Comfortable working across multiple sites and collaborating with production teams, quality engineers, and leadership alike. Fluent in English; Spanish, German or Dutch is a strong plus given our plant locations. Experience in a start-up or scale-up environment is preferred. Who You Are You are equally comfortable on a shopfloor and in a data model, and you speak both languages — the plant's and the lakehouse's. title: Customer Success Manager
description: Warum wir tun, was wir tun Unsere Psyche ist das Fenster, durch das wir die Welt sehen – mal grau, mal hell. Wer lernt, dieses Fenster zu verstehen, kann jeden Tag eine neue Perspektive gewinnen. Aus psychischen Herausforderungen können Chancen zum Wachsen werden. Und weil Glück ansteckend ist, verändert sich so die Gesellschaft: one mind at a time. Warum es diese Rolle braucht Immer mehr Arbeitgebende und Versicherungen machen Aepsy für ihre Mitarbeitenden zugänglich – vom KMU bis zum Grossunternehmen. So erhalten mehr Menschen frühzeitig Zugang zu passender psychologischer Unterstützung. Doch ein Angebot allein reicht nicht. Mitarbeitende müssen Aepsy kennen, verstehen und ihm vertrauen. Sie müssen wissen, wie sie das Angebot nutzen können, wenn sie Unterstützung brauchen. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen und sorgst dafür, dass aus Partnerschaften echte Wirkung entsteht. Dafür entwickelst du Aktivierungsmassnahmen, koordinierst Projekte und arbeitest eng mit HR-Verantwortlichen sowie unseren Teams aus Sales, Marketing, Operations und Product zusammen. Was du bewegen wirst Partnerschaften gestalten: Du betreust dein eigenes Portfolio an Partnerunternehmen, baust langfristige Beziehungen auf und verstehst, was deine Ansprechpersonen bewegt. Menschen erreichen und aktivieren: Du entwickelst Kommunikations- und Aktivierungsmassnahmen, die Mitarbeitende auf Aepsy aufmerksam machen und zur Nutzung motivieren. Projekte ins Rollen bringen: Du planst und koordinierst Projekte von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung, behältst Deadlines im Blick und bringst alle Beteiligten zusammen. Wirkung sichtbar machen: Du analysierst Aktivierungs- und Nutzungszahlen und leitest daraus konkrete Verbesserungsmassnahmen ab. Dinge besser machen: Du hinterfragst Abläufe, bringst eigene Ideen ein und entwickelst unsere Partnerschaften, Prozesse und das Produkt weiter. Was du mitbringst Du musst nicht bereits alles können. Viel wichtiger ist uns, wie du denkst, wie du mit Menschen umgehst und was dich antreibt. Erste Berufserfahrung in Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, HR oder einem verwandten Bereich. Einen Hintergrund in Psychologie oder Gesundheitsförderung ist ein Plus aber kein Muss. Freude am Aufbau von Beziehungen, Begeisterungsfähigkeit und ein ausgeprägtes Verantwortungsbewusstsein Selbstständige, strukturierte Arbeitsweise und die Fähigkeit, auch bei mehreren parallelen Projekten den Überblick zu behalten Analytisches Denken, Interesse an Zahlen und Freude daran, Prozesse zu hinterfragen und zu verbessern Freude an einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem nicht immer alles vorgegeben ist und Eigeninitiative gefragt ist Sehr gute Deutsch- sowie Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Bereitschaft, in einem 100-%-Pensum zu arbeiten und mehrheitlich vor Ort in unserem Büro im Herzen von Zürich tätig zu sein. Eine reine Remote-Tätigkeit ist nicht möglich. Was wir dir bieten Arbeit, die etwas bewirkt. Deine Arbeit hilft Menschen, psychologische Unterstützung zu finden, wenn sie sie brauchen. Du trägst dazu bei, mentale Gesundheit zugänglicher zu machen. Ein Team, das dich stärkt. Du arbeitest eng mit Sales, Marketing, Product und unserer Psycholog:innen-Community zusammen. Unterschiedliche Perspektiven, viel Know-how und eine gemeinsame Mission prägen unseren Alltag. Raum, Dinge zu bewegen. Wir wachsen und entwickeln uns weiter. Deine Ideen sind willkommen, deine Verantwortung ist real und du kannst direkt mitgestalten, wie wir unsere Partner betreuen und Mitarbeitende erreichen. Gemeinsam mit uns Wir sind ein ambitioniertes Team mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen und Überzeugungen. Wir lieben Gespräche über das grosse Ganze genauso wie über die kleinen Details. Wir glauben an das, was wir tun, und arbeiten hart für eine etwas bessere Welt. Gleichzeitig sind wir Mütter, Väter, Ehemänner und Ehefrauen, Weinliebhaber, Stand-up-Comedians, Musiker, Tänzer, Yoga-Begeisterte und Zen-Mönche, die das Leben schätzen und geniessen. Bereit, etwas zu bewegen? Schlaf darüber. Lies das Inserat nochmals. Und wenn du das Gefühl hast, dass du zu Aepsy passen könntest, freuen wir uns auf deinen Lebenslauf und ein persönliches Bewerbungsschreiben. Erzähl uns, was dich antreibt, warum dir unsere Mission wichtig ist und weshalb dich genau diese Rolle anspricht. Wir lesen jedes Schreiben aufmerksam. Build, maintain, and execute manual and automated web application test suites, using frameworks such as Cypress, Selenium, or Playwright (preferred). Build and maintain manual and automated test suites: Playwright E2E and API tests, Cypress, Selenium, integration tests against live Amazon Connect instances, and end-to-end tests of Amazon connect call flows. Caylent is an AI-first cloud services company that helps organizations turn ambitious ideas into meaningful business impact. Our capabilities span generative and agentic AI, cloud migration and modernization, cloud-native application development, data and analytics, DevOps, managed services, security and compliance, and customer experience transformation. At Caylent, our people always come first.

We are a fully remote global company with employees in Canada, the United States and Latin America. We celebrate the culture of each of our team members and foster a community of technological curiosity. Come talk to us to learn more about what it means to be a Caylien!

The Mission

This role is a Senior QA/Test Engineer specializing in Amazon Connect and contact center technology, responsible for designing and executing comprehensive test strategies across contact flows, routing, IVR/self-service, and AI-driven conversational agents. They validate legacy-to-Connect migrations, build and maintain manual and automated test suites (Playwright, Cypress, Selenium) spanning UI, API, and serverless backend components, and ensure production readiness through cutover validation, monitoring verification, and incident triage. Beyond hands-on testing, they partner with engineers to shift quality left, run UAT sessions with customer stakeholders, and contribute reusable test assets and mentorship to strengthen Caylent's contact center QA practice.

Your Assignment

Test Strategy & Contact Center Quality

  • Design and execute test strategies for Amazon Connect implementations covering contact flows, routing logic, IVR/self-service, Cases/Tasks workflows, and Contact Lens configurations
  • Build test plans that validate AI agent behavior: intent recognition accuracy, escalation paths, barge-in/fallback handling, hallucination guardrails, and multilingual/SSML voice interactions
  • Validate legacy-to-Connect migrations (i.e. Avaya, Genesys, Connect, NICE) through parallel-run testing, flow conversion verification, and data migration validation
  • Define and track quality metrics (defect density, test coverage, escape rate) and report on release readiness to delivery leads and customer stakeholders
  • Hands-on experience with web application and web automation testing

Manual, Automated & Full-Stack Testing

  • Build, maintain, and execute manual and automated IVR test suites, using tools such as Cyara, Hammer, or Botium (preferred).
  • Build, maintain, and execute manual and automated web application test suites, using frameworks such as Cypress, Selenium, or Playwright (preferred).
  • Build and maintain manual and automated test suites: Playwright E2E and API tests, Cypress, Selenium, integration tests against live Amazon Connect instances, and end-to-end tests of Amazon connect call flows.
  • Test custom Agent Workspace experiences (Amazon Connect, Agent Assist)
  • Validate serverless, event-driven backends (Lambda, EventBridge, Step Functions, SQS/SNS, DynamoDB, Kinesis) with integration and contract tests

Production Readiness & Operations

  • Execute phased rollout and cutover validation for live contact centers, where testing gaps translate directly into missed calls and customer impact
  • Verify monitoring and alerting coverage (CloudWatch metrics, alarms, dashboards) across voice, chat, tasks, queues, agents, Lambda, and AI agents prior to go-live
  • Participate in production incident triage, reproducing defects and validating fixes across the contact center stack
  • Perform security and compliance validation: least-privilege IAM checks, DevSecOps scan review, and encryption standard verification

Collaboration & Practice Contribution

  • Partner with engineers during development to shift testing left: pairing on test design, reviewing acceptance criteria, and flagging risk areas early
  • Run UAT sessions with customer stakeholders, triage findings, and drive defects to resolution ahead of production cutovers
  • Contribute reusable test assets (automated suites, test data sets, QA checklists) back to the CXE practice
  • Mentor junior QA engineers on contact center testing patterns and Caylent's quality standards

Your Qualifications

  • 8+ years of QA/test engineering experience, including 3+ years testing contact center, CCaaS, or IVR/voice platforms
  • Hands-on experience with Amazon Connect or a comparable CCaaS platform: contact flows, routing, Cases/Tasks, and reporting
  • Proficiency with automated testing frameworks (Playwright E2E and API tests, Cypress, Selenium) for unit, integration, and E2E testing
  • Experience testing serverless/event-driven AWS architectures (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Step Functions)
  • Working knowledge of conversational AI / voice testing considerations: intent accuracy, latency, fallback behavior
  • Strong defect documentation and triage skills; comfortable running UAT sessions with business and technical stakeholders
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) and integrating automated tests into deployment workflows

Preferred Qualifications

  • Contact center migration testing experience (i.e. Avaya, Genesys, Connect, NICE)
  • Experience with AI observability/trace validation (agent spans, token/cost attribution) or accessibility engineering
  • AWS certifications (Solutions Architect, Developer, or ML/Connect-relevant Specialty)
  • Contact center operations fluency: Quality management, outbound compliance, and CX KPIs
  • Consulting or client-delivery background
  • Hands on experience with Cyara Botium

title: Senior Applications Engineer (West Coast)
description: About Standard Bots Standard Bots is building the next generation of industrial robots -- hardware that's powerful, affordable, and designed to scale. We're the largest U.S. industrial robotics company by robots shipped, and our robots are showing up on factory floors everywhere from independent machine shops to NASA and Lockheed Martin. Note: This role is technically remote, but you must live on the west coast (preference for California). This job is customer-facing and requires up to 50% domestic travel, Monday through Friday. If that makes you nervous, this probably isn't the right fit. If that sounds like a perk, read on. Also note: This is not a software engineering role. If you're looking for a job where you sit at a desk and write application code, this is the wrong job description. If you want to actually build things, wire things up, and watch them run -- keep reading. The Role The Senior Applications Engineer is one of the rarest profiles in industrial automation -- and one of the most important roles at Standard Bots. You're not a mechanical engineer. You're not an electrical engineer. You're not a software engineer. You're all three, and you know how to make them talk to each other. You can look at a customer's production line, understand what's broken or slow or manual, and figure out how to fix it with a robot. Then you build the proof of concept, get on a plane, and go install it. From pre to post sale, you're the one working closely with the sales team to make the solution real. You'll build the proof of concept, design the integration, write the python scripts, build the fixture, run the wiring, and commission the cell -- then train the customer's team on how to use it. You'll also help run demos at trade shows, support trainings at customer sites and in our shop, and be the technical backbone for every customer engagement that requires hands-on expertise. This is a builder's role. Tinkerers welcome. People who get bored at a desk are strongly encouraged to apply. What You'll Do Solution Design & Proof of Concept - Work with the sales team and customers to understand automation goals, production constraints, and integration requirements - Design practical, buildable solutions around Standard Bots' hardware -- and build the proof of concept yourself to validate it works before anyone signs anything - Develop application notes, sample code, and supporting documentation that help customers and internal teams understand how to replicate and scale solutions Field Installation & Integration - Travel to customer sites to install, program, wire, and commission robotic cells - Own the integration from mechanical setup through software configuration -- fixtures, I/O, PLC handshakes, safety, test, sign-off - Troubleshoot on-site when things don't go as planned (and sometimes they don't) -- you stay until it works Customer Training & Support - Train customer operators and technicians on Standard Bots hardware and software -- both on-site and at our facility - Support customers post-install as they find new applications and push the limits of what the robot can do - Be a trusted technical resource for the accounts you've worked with -- they'll call you when something comes up Trade Shows & Demos - Represent Standard Bots at industry events and trade shows -- build the demo, run it live, talk shop with engineers and plant managers on the floor - Help develop and maintain demo systems that show the breadth of what Standard Bots hardware can do Internal Collaboration - Feed real-world integration learnings back to our hardware and software engineering teams -- you're on the front lines and your input shapes the product - Assist in-house engineering with testing new features, peripherals, and integrations as we expand the platform What We're Looking For - A genuine trifecta: you're comfortable with mechanical systems, electrical systems, and software -- not just one of the three - 6+ years of hands-on experience with industrial automation fundamentals: PLC programming and ladder logic, pneumatics, DC power systems (you know the difference between NPN and PNP), robot programming (any platform), and Python scripting - Proficiency with CAD -- SolidWorks preferred, but we care more that you can design and think in 3D than which tool you use - Customer-facing experience -- you can explain a technical integration to an engineer, a plant manager, and an ops director in the same conversation and land differently with each one - raw.jobDescription:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is building the next generation of industrial robots -- hardware that's powerful, affordable, and designed to scale. We're the largest U.S. industrial robotics company by robots shipped, and our robots are showing up on factory floors everywhere from independent machine shops to NASA and Lockheed Martin.

Note: This role is technically remote, but you must live on the west coast (preference for California). This job is customer-facing and requires up to 50% domestic travel, Monday through Friday. If that makes you nervous, this probably isn't the right fit. If that sounds like a perk, read on.

Also note: This is not a software engineering role. If you're looking for a job where you sit at a desk and write application code, this is the wrong job description. If you want to actually build things, wire things up, and watch them run -- keep reading.

The Role

The Senior Applications Engineer is one of the rarest profiles in industrial automation -- and one of the most important roles at Standard Bots.

You're not a mechanical engineer. You're not an electrical engineer. You're not a software engineer. You're all three, and you know how to make them talk to each other. You can look at a customer's production line, understand what's broken or slow or manual, and figure out how to fix it with a robot. Then you build the proof of concept, get on a plane, and go install it.

From pre to post sale, you're the one working closely with the sales team to make the solution real. You'll build the proof of concept, design the integration, write the python scripts, build the fixture, run the wiring, and commission the cell -- then train the customer's team on how to use it. You'll also help run demos at trade shows, support trainings at customer sites and in our shop, and be the technical backbone for every customer engagement that requires hands-on expertise.

This is a builder's role. Tinkerers welcome. People who get bored at a desk are strongly encouraged to apply.

What You'll Do

Solution Design & Proof of Concept

- Work with the sales team and customers to understand automation goals, production constraints, and integration requirements

- Design practical, buildable solutions around Standard Bots' hardware -- and build the proof of concept yourself to validate it works before anyone signs anything

- Develop application notes, sample code, and supporting documentation that help customers and internal teams understand how to replicate and scale solutions

Field Installation & Integration

- Travel to customer sites to install, program, wire, and commission robotic cells

- Own the integration from mechanical setup through software configuration -- fixtures, I/O, PLC handshakes, safety, test, sign-off

- Troubleshoot on-site when things don't go as planned (and sometimes they don't) -- you stay until it works

Customer Training & Support

- Train customer operators and technicians on Standard Bots hardware and software -- both on-site and at our facility

- Support customers post-install as they find new applications and push the limits of what the robot can do

- Be a trusted technical resource for the accounts you've worked with -- they'll call you when something comes up

Trade Shows & Demos

- Represent Standard Bots at industry events and trade shows -- build the demo, run it live, talk shop with engineers and plant managers on the floor

- Help develop and maintain demo systems that show the breadth of what Standard Bots hardware can do

Internal Collaboration

- Feed real-world integration learnings back to our hardware and software engineering teams -- you're on the front lines and your input shapes the product

- Assist in-house engineering with testing new features, peripherals, and integrations as we expand the platform

What We're Looking For

- A genuine trifecta: you're comfortable with mechanical systems, electrical systems, and software -- not just one of the three

- 6+ years of hands-on experience with industrial automation fundamentals: PLC programming and ladder logic, pneumatics, DC power systems (you know the difference between NPN and PNP), robot programming (any platform), and Python scripting

- Proficiency with CAD -- SolidWorks preferred, but we care more that you can design and think in 3D than which tool you use

- Customer-facing experience -- you can explain a technical integration to an engineer, a plant manager, and an ops director in the same conversation and land differently with each one

- A genuine bias for getting things done in the field, not just in theory -- you'd rather build it than write about it

- Comfort with up to 50% domestic travel; this role is hands-on and on-site by nature

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline -- or equivalent hands-on experience that tells the same story

Nice to Have

- Prior experience with collaborative robots (UR, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, or similar)

- Familiarity with machine tending, palletizing, welding, or assembly automation applications

- Experience with vision systems, force/torque sensing, or custom end-of-arm tooling

- Background in a manufacturing or production environment -- you've worked on or near a factory floor before

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $150,000 to $200,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

Company Description

Workleap is a Montreal-based tech company, founded in 2006. We're builders at heart, we make simple products that actually matter to the people who use them. We have two product lines: Workleap Agent, our newest solution built to make every manager more effective, and ShareGate, the world's leading solution for Microsoft 365 migration and governance. More than 15,000 companies worldwide trust us to do exactly that. We're intentional about who joins us. If you're the kind of person who gets excited by a hard problem and wants to help shape what comes next, there's a place for you here.

Your role

At Workleap, turning AI experiments into production capabilities is already part of how we build products and improve internal operations. Our Data team brings strong data engineering and science foundations; this role adds dedicated production AI engineering. As a Senior AI Developer, you'll design, build, and operate the AI systems and agentic workflows that connect foundation models to our data, tools, and applications, and you'll set the technical direction for how we do it well.

Your impact:

  • Ship production AI systems and agentic workflows that deliver measurable value in Workleap's products and internal operations.
  • Own the production quality of those systems: observability, testing, security, and cost built in from the start.
  • Turn evaluation evidence from Data Scientists into engineering improvements, so we know whether a system is getting better or worse.
  • Engineer the context integrations that let agents use governed data and application capabilities accurately.
  • Define reusable patterns and components so the next team starts from a working foundation, not a blank page.
  • Drive architecture decisions across quality, risk, and cost, and make the trade-offs explicit.

Your team

You'll join Workleap's Shared Tech - Data team, a hands-on team of six Data Engineers and Data Scientists responsible for the data and AI foundations supporting our products and internal teams. We value technical judgment, pragmatism, simplicity, autonomy, collaboration, and reliable delivery. You'll work closely with both disciplines and partner with Software Engineers, Product teams, and Platform and Security specialists to bring AI capabilities into production.

Over the next 6-12 months, you'll work on questions like: how does someone ask an analytical question of governed data and get an answer they can trust? How do we know an AI agent is good enough to take on more responsibility? How do we run AI features with the same rigor as any other critical system?

Our technology ecosystem includes Python, SQL, Snowflake (Cortex, Cortex Agents, Cortex Code), Claude, OpenAI, Braintrust, OpenTelemetry, Terraform, and GitHub.

What you'll bring

  • Strong production engineering in Python and SQL, with testing, CI/CD, and experience operating cloud systems;
  • Hands-on experience building and operating AI applications with foundation models, agents, tools, and context;
  • Experience instrumenting and evaluating non-deterministic systems: observability, evals, regression testing;
  • Sound architectural judgment across reliability, security, and cost, and the confidence to form and defend a technical opinion;
  • Experience building components or tooling that other developers adopt;
  • Working knowledge of Snowflake and its AI capabilities (Cortex), or the ability to ramp up on them quickly;
  • A builder mindset: you own what you ship, experiment quickly, and use AI-assisted development tools daily and critically;
  • Bonus: AI services on Azure, AWS, or GCP, or developer platforms that accelerate AI adoption across teams.

Most of this sounds like you? Apply.

What the job comes with

  • Base salary: $140 000 - $170 000. This range reflects our Canada-wide compensation scale. Final offers may be adjusted based on the candidate's region to align with local market conditions.
  • Annual bonus program.
  • LTIP program, share in Workleap's long-term growth.
  • RRSP + Family health insurance + telemedicine + annual wellness budget.
  • Flexible vacation policy.
  • Remote work, with access to our Montreal office.
  • In-person gatherings twice a year.
  • Claude access, for everyone.

What drives us

At Workleap, we build software that sits at the center of how people experience work, every day, at every level.

We move fast. Priorities shift, decisions get made with the information we have, and we iterate. If you thrive on intensity and ambiguity doesn't slow you down, you'll feel right at home.
We're builders. We do what it takes to move forward. AI is part of our toolkit. We use it to go faster and decide smarter, not to replace judgment.

If you want real impact and a place where your decisions matter, this is it.

How we hire

Transparency is how we hire — for you as much as for us.

Here's how it works: a first call with a recruiter, then a virtual interview with the hiring manager. You'll then complete a take-home case study, followed by a meet with future colleagues to discuss it together. Depending on the role, the process may vary slightly — your recruiter will walk you through it on your first call.

We use AI to support certain steps of the process, but every hiring decision remains human.

We can't wait to meet you.

By applying, you confirm that you have read and agree to our privacy policy.

title: CDI - Senior Product Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

 

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

 

Processus de recrutement

Le processus demande environ quatre heures, réparties en six étapes dont une seule sur site.

  1. Entretien RH (45 min, à distance) : parcours, motivations et points pratiques, comme le calendrier et les prétentions salariales.

  2. Appel avec le CTO (15 à 30 min, à distance).

  3. Screening technique (30 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter AI Applied Engineer) : retour détaillé sur vos projets passés, puis questions techniques et de design de solution.

  4. Code review et live coding (60 min, sur site, avec un membre du chapter) : relecture d’un dépôt de code existant et correction de ses défauts, puis construction d’une nouvelle fonctionnalité avec un coding agent et présentation du résultat.

  5. Cas technique (45 min, à distance, avec un membre du chapter) : cadrage d’un problème métier, proposition d’une solution technique, description de la méthode d’évaluation, puis discussion de vos choix.

  6. Entretien final (30 min, à distance, avec une personne de l’encadrement du département, Engineering Manager ou Director) : reprise des points restés ouverts, choix de l’archétype et du niveau les mieux adaptés à votre profil, et réponses à toutes vos questions.

Selon les étapes, tous les outils d’IA sont autorisés, ou aucun. Lors du live coding, c’est la manière de travailler avec l’assistance de l’IA qui est observée.

 

Rémunération : 60 000€ à 70 000€ brut annuel (fixe) + jusqu’à 6 000€ de variable selon expérience et séniorité

 

Chez Artefact, nous sommes convaincus que la diversité des parcours, des expériences et des perspectives fait la richesse de nos équipes. Nous nous engageons à offrir un environnement inclusif et des opportunités équitables, où chacune et chacun peut évoluer et exprimer pleinement son potentiel. Nos recrutements reposent sur les compétences, le potentiel et l’adéquation avec le rôle.

title: Campaign Analyst
description: Onze missie is helder: beter eten voor meer mensen bereikbaar maken. Als Campaign Analyst in het Customer Retention team speel je hierin een cruciale rol door onze klanten beter vast te houden. Jij zorgt ervoor dat we al onze verhalen, over al onze producten, op de juiste manier aan de juiste klant vertellen. Je bent continu, datagedreven op zoek naar verbetering; zodat we het volgende verhaal nóg beter vertellen. Wat je gaat doen Onze retentiestrategie wordt steeds geavanceerder. We sturen niet simpelweg 'een korting' naar alle klanten maar werken met gelaagde acties, inspirerende verhalen en gepersonaliseerde extra’s. Enerzijds ben jij de analytische drijfkracht achter de executie van onze campagnes. Je bouwt, beheert en verbetert de analytische tooling en dashboards zodat we kunnen blijven leren. Daarmee creëer je begrip van - en grip op - de commerciële impact van campagnes, en alle onderliggende onderdelen (zoals kanaalstrategie, product-samenstelling of klantdoelgroep). Vervolgens vertaal je de verworven inzichten effectief naar succesfactoren, verbeteringstrajecten en/of toekomstige experimenten. Anderzijds werk je inhoudelijk mee. Je bepaalt samen met de Campaign Specialist welk aanbod naar welke klanten gaat, via welk kanaal en met welke verwachting en zet je ook (nieuwe) acties zelf op. Een aantal van jouw verantwoordelijkheden: Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de performance van campagnes. Je analyseert de impact, en je gebruikt inzichten om toekomstige campagnes te verbeteren, zodat we kunnen blijven innoveren in onze retentiestrategie. Je werkt actief mee met het team: je levert niet alleen de inzichten, maar bent ook zelf verantwoordelijk voor de implementatie van campagnes. Je bepaalt en draait de experimentagenda: welke hypotheses testen we over aanbod, doelgroep en kanaal, en wat leren we ervan? Je bouwt, onderhoudt en verbetert zelf de datamodellen (SQL/dbt) en dashboards (Data Studio) waarop het team stuurt. Dit ben jij Je hebt een afgeronde WO of HBO-opleiding op zak. Je hebt 2-5 jaar ervaring met marketing (intelligence) en data/business analytics. Je spreekt en schrijft vloeiend Nederlands. Je bent analytisch sterk en je werkt datagedreven en gestructureerd. Je kunt vloeiend SQL, hebt ervaring met het maken van dashboards en datamodellen en je gebruikt graag AI-tools om je werk efficiënter te maken. Ervaring met dbt is een pré. Je hebt ervaring met A/B-tests, holdout-tests en hypothese gedreven werken. Je hebt commercieel gevoel: je denkt net zo graag mee over het aanbod als over de cijfers erachter. Je bent een sterke sparringpartner: je daagt collega’s uit met data en laat je zelf ook uitdagen. Je bent kritisch, hands-on en niet bang om de status quo uit te dagen. Wat wij bieden Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem. 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden. Een extra vrije dag per jaar om je in te zetten voor vrijwilligerswerk en iets goeds te doen. Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp. Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL. Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University. Je bent continu, datagedreven op zoek naar verbetering; zodat we het volgende verhaal nóg beter vertellen.

Onze retentiestrategie wordt steeds geavanceerder. We sturen niet simpelweg 'een korting' naar alle klanten maar werken met gelaagde acties, inspirerende verhalen en gepersonaliseerde extra’s.
